superseded_asset.preservation: retained unchanged as a valid zero-provider design/qualification asset; prohibited as the R4 execution split

surviving_asset.qualification: 378/378 golden self-check and 378/378 blank-init negative control PASS
surviving_asset.e1: 12 family-homogeneous independently evolved streams, exactly two streams per precommitted structural procedure family and eight tasks per stream
surviving_asset.e3: 12 family-homogeneous sealed future streams, exactly two streams per precommitted structural procedure family and eight tasks per stream
surviving_asset.common_probe: 18 never-fed tasks, exactly three per structural procedure family

preoutcome_reason.problem_in_v1: The v1 E1 streams were outcome-blind but mixed all six structural procedure families. They could identify an overall projection effect, but an updater consumes an eight-trajectory batch nonlinearly, so a mixed stream cannot identify a family-conditional diagnostic advantage delta_z or support a clean prospective family ranking.
preoutcome_reason.repair_in_v2: Keep the same six-family controlled task generator and L9 factor design, add one sealed future block, and freeze E1/E3 streams to one structural procedure family each. This changes only pre-outcome allocation and identifiability, not the scientific headline or observed results.
preoutcome_reason.why_not_posthoc: No actor, updater, probe, or benchmark model outcome existed for either suite when this supersession was made. The issue was discovered while compiling the formal R4 estimand from the four-round review requirements.

frozen_partition.partition_variable: primary structural procedure family assigned by the generator before any model call
frozen_partition.actual_failure_codes: may be logged descriptively but cannot replace or redefine the primary partition
